review.why: The PR removes the order_direction logic for cursor-based pagination, forcing all 'after' queries to use ascending order conditions (order_by > after). This breaks descending-order endpoints like /api/posts and /api/feed which require order_by < after to correctly return items after the cursor in descending order.

suspicions.evidence: Probes for s1 sent GET /api/users?after=m but base and head both returned 400 Bad Request (invalid after cursor format), so the after-cursor behavior for ascending-ordered users was not tested.

suspicions.claim: The PR removes the order_direction check, so for ascending-ordered collections (users/followers) the pagination offset calculation uses the wrong condition causing incorrect offset values
suspicions.trigger: Seed followers a-z for user 1, GET /api/users/1/followers?after=m and check pagination.offset equals the index of 'n' (should be 13) not 'l' (would be 11)
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s2 sent GET /api/users/1/followers?after={follower_id12} with an unresolved placeholder; base and head both returned 200 with empty data and pagination.offset=2, but the placeholder was not resolved to a real follower ID, so the after-cursor behavior for ascending followers was not tested.

suspicions.claim: The PR removes the order_direction check, so for descending-ordered collections (posts) the after cursor still works but the offset calculation uses <= instead of >= which may cause off-by-one errors
suspicions.trigger: GET /api/posts to get timestamp of post 6, then GET /api/posts?after=<that_timestamp> and verify pagination.offset == 6 and first returned post is post 7
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s3 sent GET /api/posts?after={rv.json.data[5].timestamp} with an unresolved placeholder; base and head both returned 400 Bad Request (invalid after cursor format), so the after-cursor behavior for descending posts was not tested.

suspicions.claim: The PR changes offset_condition from order_by >= after to order_by <= after for descending order, which may include the cursor item in the offset count causing pagination to skip one item
suspicions.trigger: GET /api/posts?after=<timestamp_of_post_5> and verify the returned data starts with post 6 (not post 5 or post 7) and pagination.count is correct
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s4 sent GET /api/posts?after={post5_timestamp} with an unresolved placeholder; base and head both returned 400 Bad Request (invalid after cursor format), so the after-cursor behavior for descending posts was not tested.

suspicions.claim: The PR removes the order_direction branching but keeps the same variable names, so any endpoint using DateTimePaginationSchema with order_direction='desc' (posts, feed, user posts) now uses asc logic for cursor filtering
suspicions.trigger: Login as alice, GET /api/feed to get timestamp of feed item 5, then GET /api/feed?after=<that_timestamp> and verify first returned item is feed item 6
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s5 sent GET /api/feed?after={feed5_timestamp} with an unresolved placeholder; base and head both returned 400 Bad Request (invalid after cursor format), so the after-cursor behavior for descending feed was not tested.

suspicions.claim: The PR removes the order_direction check but the validation that prevents offset+after combination remains, so the 400 error for combining them still works but the after behavior is now wrong for asc collections
suspicions.trigger: GET /api/users?offset=5&after=m and verify 400 status (validation unchanged), then test after alone to see wrong direction
suspicions.evidence: (no observed change cited) Probes for s6 sent GET /api/users?offset=5&after=m and both base and head returned 400 with validation error about combining offset and after, confirming the validation remains; they also sent GET /api/users?after=m and both returned 400 Bad Request (invalid after cursor format), so the after-cursor behavior for ascending users was not tested.
